'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Insurgency in the Maghreb (2002–present)|Insurgency in the Maghreb]]
**[[2021 Tillabéri attacks]]
***Seven members of the electoral commission are killed and three others are wounded in a [[land mine]] explosion in [[Tillabéri]], [[Niger]]. The attack is carried out on the same day as the [[2020–21 Nigerien general election|second round of the presidential election]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-56148942 (BBC News)]
*[[Libyan Crisis (2011–present)|Libyan Crisis]]
**[[United Nations|UN]]-backed [[Ministry of Interior (Libya)|Libyan Minister of the Interior]] [[Fathi Bashagha]] escapes a motorcade shooting in [[Tripoli, Libya|Tripoli]]. One of his guards is wounded and the others chase the assailants, killing one of them and arresting two others. The ministry calls the attack an [[assassination]] attempt. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/spokesman-libyan-minister-survives-attack-motorcade-76030770 (ABC News)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*A [[Nigerian Air Force]] [[King Air 350]] [[military plane]] crashes on approach to [[Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport]] in [[Abuja]], [[Nigeria]], killing all seven people on board. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-nigeria-crash/nigerian-military-plane-crashes-on-approach-to-abuja-airport-minister-idUSKBN2AL0BL?il=0 (Reuters)]
*A [[Mexican Air Force]] [[Learjet 45]] jet crashes in [[Emiliano Zapata Municipality, Veracruz|Emiliano Zapata Municipality]], [[Veracruz]], killing six crew members. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mexico-airplane-crash/six-killed-in-mexican-air-force-plane-accident-in-veracruz-idUSKBN2AL0MP?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Israel]]i authorities close off access to its [[Mediterranean Sea|Mediterranean]] beaches following an [[2021 Israel oil spill|offshore oil spill]] that has devastated more than {{convert|100|mi}} of the country's coastline. The [[Israel Nature and Parks Authority]] calls the spill "one of the most serious ecological disasters" in the country’s history. The cause of the spill is currently under investigation. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/israel-shuts-mediterranean-shore-after-oil-devastates-coast-israel-jerusalem-oil-beaches-mediterranean-b1805277.html (''The Independent'')]

'''Health and environment''' 
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Israel]]
****[[Israel]] reopens many sectors of their [[Economy of Israel|economy]] as part of an easing of [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] restrictions. However, while shops are open to all residents, access to leisure sites is limited to people who have received a [[vaccine]] or who have recovered from [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/middle-east/20210221-israel-starts-reopening-as-covid-19-vaccination-rate-nears-50 (France 24)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****[[Malaysia]] receives its first shipment of 312,390 doses of the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|Pfizer–BioNTech vaccine]]. This allows the starting date of the vaccination campaign to be brought forward to February 24. [https://www.malaymail.com/news/malaysia/2021/02/21/first-shipment-of-pfizer-biontech-covid-19-vaccine-arrives-in-malaysia/1951544 (''Malay Mail'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]], [[Lineage B.1.1.7]]
****The [[Philippines]] confirms 18 new cases of the B.1.1.7 variant of [[Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2|SARS-CoV-2]] first detected in the [[United Kingdom]]. [https://www.cnnphilippines.com/news/2021/2/21/b117-variant-covid19-new-cases.html (CNN Philippines)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Taiwan]], [[Lineage P.1]]
****[[Taiwan]] confirms their first three cases of the Lineage P.1 variant of [[Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2|SARS-CoV-2]] first detected in [[Brazil]], prompting the [[Government of the Republic of China|government]] to impose a 14-day [[quarantine]] for all travelers arriving from Brazil at a centralized facility beginning February 24. [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/east-asia/taiwan-confirms-three-cases-of-brazil-covid-19-variant (''The Straits Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New York (state)|COVID-19 pandemic in New York]], [[501.V2 variant]]
****[[New York (state)|New York]] reports their first case of the 501.V2 variant from [[South Africa]] in a person from [[Nassau County, New York|Nassau County]]. [https://www.cnbc.com/2021/02/21/south-africa-covid-variant-detected-in-first-new-york-patient.html (CNBC)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
****[[Australia]] begins a [[COVID-19 vaccination in Australia|mass vaccination campaign]] with the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|Pfizer–BioNTech vaccine]]. [[Prime Minister of Australia|Prime Minister]] [[Scott Morrison]] is one of the first people to receive a vaccine. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-02-21/australia-covid-vaccinations-begin-first-shots-administered/13176288 (ABC Australia)]
***Australia and [[New Zealand]] reopen their maritime borders after recent outbreaks in both countries have been contained. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2021/feb/20/victoria-records-zero-new-coronavirus-cases-as-melbourne-case-moved-to-icu (''The Guardian'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina]]
***[[Argentina]] approves the emergency use of [[Sinopharm]]'s [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. [https://www.latercera.com/que-pasa/noticia/argentina-aprobo-uso-de-la-vacuna-china-contra-coronavirus-sars-cov-2/XMGCMK5IVFCRTM65ZEKSUH2S2M/ (''La Tercera'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Serbia]]
***[[Serbia]] receives their first shipment of 150,000 doses of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]], making it the first country in the [[Western Balkan]] region to receive vaccines. [https://rs.n1info.com/vesti/vakcine-astrazeneke-stigle-u-srbiju/ (N1)]

'''International relations'''
*The [[International Atomic Energy Agency]] reaches an agreement with [[Iran]] to allow inspectors to resume monitoring their [[Nuclear program of Iran|nuclear program]] for up to three months. However, the agreement bars inspectors from doing snap inspections and also prohibits them from reviewing footage taken at the nuclear sites. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/2/21/iaea-iran-agree-temporary-deal-inspections-access (Al Jazeera)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2020–21 Nigerien general election]]
**[[Niger]]iens vote in a runoff to select a new [[President of Niger|president]], in what is considered to be the nation's first potential [[peaceful transition of power]] since gaining independence in 1960. The two candidates are the ruling [[Nigerien Party for Democracy and Socialism]]'s leader [[Mohamed Bazoum]], and former president [[Mahamane Ousmane]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-niger-election/niger-votes-in-presidential-runoff-to-usher-in-first-democratic-transition-idUSKBN2AL00R?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[2021 Ecuadorian general election]]
**The National Electoral Council confirms that [[Creating Opportunities|CREO]] candidate [[Guillermo Lasso]] will face the winner of the first round [[Andrés Arauz]] in the runoff. [https://cnnespanol.cnn.com/2021/02/21/elecciones-ecuador-guillermo-lasso-segunda-vuelta/ (CNN in Spanish)]
*[[2021 Laotian parliamentary election]]
**[[Laotians]] vote in a parliamentary election to elect the members of the [[National Assembly (Laos)|ninth National Assembly]]. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2021-02/21/c_139756841.htm (''Xinhuanet'')]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[2021 Myanmar protests]], aftermath of the [[2021 Myanmar coup d'état]]
**[[Facebook]] takes down the main page of the [[Tatmadaw|military]] of [[Myanmar]] a day after two protesters were killed. The [[social media]] site said that the account violated its policies of "incitement to violence and coordinating harm". Earlier, the military had blocked Internet access in many parts of the country. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-56144904 (BBC News)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2021 Australian Open]]
**[[Novak Djokovic]] defeats [[Daniil Medvedev]] in the final to win the [[2021 Australian Open – Men's Singles|Men's Singles]] competition of the tournament. [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/02/21/sports/tennis/novak-djokovic-wins-australian-open.html (''The New York Times'')]
**[[Ivan Dodig]] and [[Filip Polášek]] win the [[2021 Australian Open – Men's Doubles|Men's Doubles]] by defeating [[Rajeev Ram]] and [[Joe Salisbury]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-tennis-ausopen-doubles/dodig-polasek-win-australian-open-mens-doubles-title-idUSKBN2AL055 (Reuters)]
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in Rwanda]], [[impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports]]
**[[Rwanda]] will allow individual and non-contact outdoor sports activities to resume on February 23 due to a decline in the number of COVID-19 cases. [https://www.newtimes.co.rw/sports/individual-non-contact-outdoor-sports-activities-resume (''New Times'')]
